newsitem.title: USA: Gillette Duracell unit Q4 net drops.
newsitem.headline: Gillette Duracell unit Q4 net drops.

text.p: Gillette Co said on Friday that before one-time, merger-related costs, sales for its Duracell unit rose in the fourth quarter, but before one-time, merger-related costs, profits were slightly lower.
According to Gillette, sales and profit growth for Duracell was constrained by temporary distribution dislocations associated with the merger.
Gillette reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.72 a share, before merger-related costs on sales of $3.0 billion, compared to $0.64 a share on sales of $2.7 billion the previous fourth quarter.
The company said its blade and razor sales for the fourth quarter rose "well above" the prior year's comparable period, while profits increased "sharply".
Sales of Braun products were "substantially" higher in the quarter, compared with a year ago, it said.

According to the company, toiletries and cosmetics sales in the fourth quarter rose "considerably" versus the prior year, while profits were "moderately" lower. The lower profit reflected launch costs of new products and the geographic expansion of Gillette Series men's grooming products and Satin Care female shaving products in Europe, Gillette said.
Sales of stationery products in the quarter moved "notably" higher, and profits were up "substantially" over those of last year.
Oral-B products sales and profits for fourth quarter "strongly" surpassed those of 1995.
